question: A molecular biologist is studying the roles of different types of ion channels regulating cardiac excitation. He identifies a voltage-gated calcium channel in the sinoatrial node, which is also present throughout the myocardium. The channel is activated at ~ -40 mV of membrane potential, undergoes voltage-dependent inactivation, and is highly sensitive to nifedipine. Which of the following phases of the action potential in the sinoatrial node is primarily mediated by ion currents through the channel that the molecular biologist is studying?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Voltage-gated calcium channel activation at ~ -40 mV -> Mediates the upstroke of the action potential (Phase 0) in the sinoatrial node -> 80% confidence. CHAIN: Voltage-gated calcium channel undergoes voltage-dependent inactivation -> Contributes to the plateau phase (Phase 2) of the action potential in the sinoatrial node -> 75% confidence. CHAIN: Sensitivity to nifedipine indicates involvement in the repolarization phase (Phase 3) of the action potential in the sinoatrial node -> 80%
enhanced_information: The voltage-gated calcium channel in the sinoatrial node mediates the upstroke of the action potential (Phase 0) and contributes to the plateau phase (Phase 2). Its sensitivity to nifedipine indicates involvement in the repolarization phase (Phase 3). Therefore, the ion currents through this channel primarily mediate Phase 0 of the action potential in the sinoatrial node.
analysis: The voltage-gated calcium channel identified in the sinoatrial node primarily mediates Phase 0 of the action potential. This channel is responsible for the upstroke of the action potential in the cardiac pacemaker cells.
